subject: Integration debt — request for trial grace period
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex@acmeanalytics.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0500
Subject: Request: brief grace period due to integration debt

Hi Priya and Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited by Redwood's latency numbers and the hosted routing options. We're in the middle of wiring the data plane to our event router and hit an unexpected set of integration-debt items that will push our POC readiness out by ~3 weeks.

We have a hard internal demo with the execs on Dec 18; to make meaningful progress for that demo we need an additional 30 days of trial runway and a small token supplement so our devs can run end-to-end tests without interruptions.

I've attached the short integration log and a checklist that shows the blockers. Can Redwood provide a 30-day trial grace period and a sandbox top-up (~$6k equivalent) while we finish the adapter work? If helpful, I can move the demo but the exec alignment would be best if we keep the date.

Appreciate any flexibility — we really want to validate Redwood in-production flows.

Alex Rivera
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Analytics
attachments: integration_log_20261129.txt, poc_integration_checklist.xlsx

Subject: Re: Request: brief grace period due to integration debt

Alex — thanks for the detail and for sharing the log. I copied our solutions lead (Kim) and Ben (sales lead) so we can move quickly.

Short answer: yes, we should be able to extend the trial window while engineering finishes the adapter. A couple of asks so we can route this internally fast:
- Can you confirm the minimum additional runway you need (30 days vs 45)?
- Is the $6k figure total estimated token cost or engineering effort cost? We typically top up tokens but can also provide a limited credit for engineering validation.
- Any IP/data residency concerns we should note for the private endpoints?

Kim: can you review the attached checklist and confirm whether our sandbox capacity and logging configuration will be sufficient for their planned E2E tests?

I'll open an internal approval thread and aim to have a decision within 24 business hours.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

Priya / team — I reviewed Alex's integration checklist and log (thanks Alex). The blockers look like:
- Event schema mismatch between their router and our ingestion adapters (needs one small transform)
- Auth rotation delay for their staging keys (developer-side)
- A single curl-level flaky endpoint that's causing retries (we can mitigate with a short-lived retry policy)

From a sandbox capacity perspective, they don't need anything special beyond token top-up; our hosted sandboxes will support the E2E tests. I recommend: 30-day extension + $5k token credit (enough for their stated test volume) and I can provide a quick runbook for the retry policy and a short transform snippet.

If Ben is comfortable with the $5k credit we can approve and I will attach the runbook and schedule a 30-min sync with their engineers.

—Kim
Kimberly Park
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
